name: Applied Leadership, BA
description: In collaboration with the School of Business, the School of Graduate and Continuing Studies offers a BA in applied leadership. The program prepares adult learners who are seeking a degree-completion program to move into areas of greater responsibility and accountability in their organizations through an interdisciplinary curriculum that explores human behavior and its application to leadership. This curriculum is rooted in Christian virtues and practices and includes relevant theory and principles. In addition to the requirements of the major, students also must satisfy the requirements of the degree-completion Core curriculum.

requirements.name: Core Requirements
requirements.description: FOUNDATIONS Community and Commitments: 2 hours CORE 100 Foundations of Christianity I: 4 hours REL 121 or REL 131 Foundations of Christianity II - at least 2 hours Course listings for this category may be found here. COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS Foundational Writing: ENGL 101 OR ENGL 100 and ENGL 102 Health and Movement: 1 hour Course listings for this category may be found here. World Languages I: 3 hours High school exemption from World Languages I is possible. To obtain a high school exemption, a student must complete three sequential years in the same language with a B or better for each semester. IDIS 101 KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING Complete coursework totaling at least 18 semester hours from at least five of the six Knowledge and Understanding categories, including at least 2 semester hours from each of the following categories: Arts, Oral Rhetoric, Visual Rhetoric; Humanities; Social and Behavioral Sciences. Course listings for each category may be found here. World Languages II: 0-4 hours Arts, Oral Rhetoric, Visual Rhetoric: 2-6 hours Humanities: 2-6 hours Mathematical Sciences: 0-4 hours Natural Sciences: 0-6 hours Social and Behavioral Sciences: 2-6 hours CROSS-DISCIPLINARY INTEGRATION Engaged Citizenship Commitments Complete at least one tagged course in all four areas. These courses may also satisfy other core requirements. The full list of approved courses may be found here. Diversity and Difference Environmental Sustainability Global Regions and Cultures Rhetoric in the Disciplines Contemporary Challenges and Enduring Questions: 4 hours GCS 391 (Grand Rapids Campus) or ML 326 (Handlon Campus)
